page: Microsoft Azure F2ads_v7 is an entry-tier compute-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 1 thread per core without hyperthreading concurrency, backed by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 8.0 GB, providing an even 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. A key architectural attribute is the inclusion of 236 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage. The instance operates without discrete GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional single-thread compute capabilities, placing its stress-ng single-core score of 3771.98 in the top tier of comparable instances. The CPU architecture supports extended vector instruction sets, including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, contributing to top-decile gzip compression rates of 41.41 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression of 18.24 GB/sec. Conversely, overall multithreaded capacity is strictly bounded by the two-core ceiling. Multi-core stress-ng registers an average score of 7502.15, while multithreaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput register in the lower performance quartiles.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F2ads_v7 delivers an advantageous profile for compute-bound tasks that do not scale across wide core fabrics but require peak clock rates and low-latency local scratch disk space. The bundled NVMe volume avoids remote block storage overhead for temporary files. Primary tradeoffs center on the low aggregate core count and limited memory ceiling, making the VM ill-fitted for heavy parallel data processing or memory-intensive machine learning inference. The instance is best suited for single-threaded utilities, batch compression, CI/CD pipeline workers, and lightweight caching or proxy services.
description: Microsoft Azure F2ads_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by a 2-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz with a 1:1 physical-to-virtual CPU mapping. It provides 8.0 GB of memory and includes a bundled 236 GB local NVMe SSD, operating without dedicated GPU hardware. Benchmark results reflect top-tier single-core throughput and accelerated compression routines enabled by extensive AVX-512 vector support. With only two dedicated threads, multithreaded execution and web serving throughput remain at moderate levels. The instance offers a balanced, cost-effective resource footprint for tasks prioritizing individual core frequency and local ephemeral disk speed over wide parallel scaling, making it well suited for lightweight batch jobs, code compilation tasks, caching layers, and CI/CD agent execution.
